SkyTruth Analysis

Reported Spill Volume: 200 gallons
Report Description
*****WEB REPORT**** ON 02/24/2013 AT 1903 HOURS, HARDIN COUNTY, ADVISED A "PASSER-BY" REPORTED A DIESEL FUEL LEAK FROM A TRAIN THAT WAS STOPPED AT MP QT 72.23 ON THE TOLEDO BRANCH SUBDIVISION. THIS IS LOCATED NEAR THE MAIN STREET CROSSING IN KENTON, OH. ID TRAIN DISPATCHER WAS NOTIFIED CSX CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED AND REQUESTED FOLLOW UP INFORMATION AND CONFIRMATION FROM RESPONDING POLICE AND FIRE UNITS. HARDIN COUNTY WAS ASKED TO CALL CSX WITH CONFIRMATION OF FUEL LEAK FROM ON SCENE UNITS WHEN AVAILABLE. UPDATE: AT 1916 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED FIRE UNITS AND TRAIN CREW WERE INSPECTING TRAIN H71824 AND ADVISED PSCC WOULD BE NOTIFIED OF FINDINGS. UPDATE: AT 1928 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM THE INSPECTION HOLE ON LOCOMOTIVE CSXT 2522 ON TRAIN H71824. IT WAS BELIEVED THE LEAK RESULTED FROM THE TANK HAVING BEEN OVERFILLED BY 200 GALLON TODAY BEFORE THEY LEFT THE YARD. THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS ON-SCENE, AND THEY WERE MOVING THE TRAIN TO A NEARBY "STUB TRACK". UPDATE: AT 1932 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE FUEL LEAK HAS STOPPED DUE TO THE OVERFLOW COMPLETELY SPILLING OUT. FIRE DEPARTMENT PUT DOWN TRACK PADS AND HAD LEFT THE SCENE. UPDATE: AT 1937 HOURS, HARDIN COUNTY, ADVISED RESPONDING FIRE UNITS REPORTED APPROXIMATELY TWO GALLONS LEAKED ONTO A TWO FOOT-BY-TWO FOOT AREA, WHICH THE LOCAL FIRE UNITS SECURED WITH ABSORBENT PADS. HARDIN COUNTY ADVISED ON SCENE FIRE UNITS REPORTED THERE WAS NO NEED FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES FOR THIS ISSUE AND THE TRAIN WAS BEING RELEASED. CSX CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED.

*****WEB REPORT**** ON 02/24/2013 AT 1903 HOURS, HARDIN COUNTY, ADVISED A "PASSER-BY" REPORTED A DIESEL FUEL LEAK FROM A TRAIN THAT WAS STOPPED AT MP QT 72.23 ON THE TOLEDO BRANCH SUBDIVISION. THIS IS LOCATED NEAR THE MAIN STREET CROSSING IN KENTON, OH. ID TRAIN DISPATCHER WAS NOTIFIED CSX CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED AND REQUESTED FOLLOW UP INFORMATION AND CONFIRMATION FROM RESPONDING POLICE AND FIRE UNITS. HARDIN COUNTY WAS ASKED TO CALL CSX WITH CONFIRMATION OF FUEL LEAK FROM ON SCENE UNITS WHEN AVAILABLE. UPDATE: AT 1916 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED FIRE UNITS AND TRAIN CREW WERE INSPECTING TRAIN H71824 AND ADVISED PSCC WOULD BE NOTIFIED OF FINDINGS. UPDATE: AT 1928 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE LEAK WAS COMING FROM THE INSPECTION HOLE ON LOCOMOTIVE CSXT 2522 ON TRAIN H71824. IT WAS BELIEVED THE LEAK RESULTED FROM THE TANK HAVING BEEN OVERFILLED BY 200 GALLON TODAY BEFORE THEY LEFT THE YARD. THE LOCAL FIRE DEPARTMENT WAS ON-SCENE, AND THEY WERE MOVING THE TRAIN TO A NEARBY "STUB TRACK". UPDATE: AT 1932 HOURS, ID TRAIN DISPATCHER ADVISED THE FUEL LEAK HAS STOPPED DUE TO THE OVERFLOW COMPLETELY SPILLING OUT. FIRE DEPARTMENT PUT DOWN TRACK PADS AND HAD LEFT THE SCENE. UPDATE: AT 1937 HOURS, HARDIN COUNTY, ADVISED RESPONDING FIRE UNITS REPORTED APPROXIMATELY TWO GALLONS LEAKED ONTO A TWO FOOT-BY-TWO FOOT AREA, WHICH THE LOCAL FIRE UNITS SECURED WITH ABSORBENT PADS. HARDIN COUNTY ADVISED ON SCENE FIRE UNITS REPORTED THERE WAS NO NEED FOR ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES FOR THIS ISSUE AND THE TRAIN WAS BEING RELEASED. CSX CRISIS COMMUNICATIONS MANAGER, WAS NOTIFIED.

Reported Spill Volume: 1 gallon
Report Description
****WEB REPORT**** DFD WAS CALLED BY WAL-MART LOSS PREVENTION PERSONNEL IN REFERENCE TO A POSSIBLE DIESEL SPILL IN THEIR PARKING LOT. DFD RESPONDED AND FOUND A SLICK OF OIL OR DIESEL FUEL WHICH THEY SAID HAD LEAKED OUT OF A TRUCK WHICH WAS NO LONGER AT THE STORE. ANOTHER CAR WAS PARKED IN THE SPOT AND THEY WERE WORRIED ABOUT POSSIBLE IGNITION OR DAMAGE TO THE NEW CAR. DFD USED A COMMERCIAL ABSORBENT TO CLEAN UP WHAT WAS LEFT OF THE SPILL, WHICH WAS LESS THAN 1 LITER. THE SPILL HAD RUN INTO A STORM DRAIN, BUT WAS NO LONGER FLOWING AND IT DID NOT APPEAR THAT MUCH HAD GOTTEN INTO THE DRAIN. CITY OF DOUGLAS PUBLIC WORKS WAS CONTACTED AND ADVISED OF THE SITUATION IN CASE THEY WANTED TO INVESTIGATE FURTHER. THE ABSORBENT AND MATERIAL WERE SWEPT UP (APPROXIMATELY .5 CUBIC FEET OF MATERIAL) AND TAKEN BACK TO DFD FOR PROPER DISPOSAL.

Suspected Responsible Party: B&N FISHERIES
Skytruth Analysis
Reported Sheen Size: 2 feet by 100 feet (area 200 sq. ft.)
Reported Spill Volume: 9 gallons
Skytruth Minimum Possible Spill Volume: 0 gallons
WHILE DOCKING AT TRIDENT SEAFOODS DOCK IN AKUTAN AK, THE VESSEL BUMPED INTO THE DOCK WHERE A BUMPER ON THE DOCK WAS MISSING. THERE WAS A SMALL PIECE OF STEEL ROD STICKING OUT FROM TEH DOCK FAR ENOUGH TO HIT THE SIDE OF THE BOAT. ON IMPACT THE ROD PUNCTURED THE #1 STRBD FUEL TANK CAUSING A SMALL CRACK IN THE HULL. WHILE THE FISH WAS BEING UNLOADED FROM THE VESSEL THE VESSEL LISTED FAR ENOUGH TO STARBOARD TO ALLOW FUEL TO LEAK OUT INTO THE WATER. THE VESSEL WAS RIGHTED AND THE FUEL DISCHARGE WAS STOPPED, THE FUEL WAS CONTAINED TO THE DOCK SIDE OF THE VESSEL WITH OIL BOOM AND A COMPLETE CLEAN-UP WAS POSSIBLE WITH ABSORBENT BOOMS AND DIAPERS.
